headline: Profit falls on tough comparisons, but guidance rises
summary_short: AEP's Q2 2026 GAAP EPS fell to $1.31 from $2.29 a year ago (net income $713M vs $1,226M) mainly on the absence of large prior-year one-off items, even as revenue rose 7.0% y/y to $5,445 million; the company raised full-year 2026 operating EPS guidance to $6.25-$6.55 from $6.15-$6.45.
summary_long: Second-quarter GAAP earnings fell to $713 million ($1.31/share) from $1,226 million ($2.29/share) a year earlier, primarily reflecting the absence of two 2025 items: a transmission minority-interest sale benefit at AEP Transmission Holdco and a FERC NOLC order gain. Operating (non-GAAP) earnings were roughly flat at $742 million ($1.36/share) versus $766 million ($1.43/share), as new item disallowances (WVPSC order, Pirkey Plant, Unified Tracker Mechanism) and wholesale customer contract agreements only partly offset segment growth. Revenue rose 7.0% y/y to $5,445 million on higher commercial and industrial demand. AEP raised full-year 2026 operating EPS guidance to $6.25-$6.55 from $6.15-$6.45, citing strong first-half performance, and reaffirmed its 7%-9% long-term annual growth rate.

drivers.explanation: GAAP earnings fell y/y mainly because 2025 included a transmission minority-interest sale gain and a FERC NOLC order benefit that did not recur in 2026, per the release's own reconciliation tables.
Total retail and wholesale KWh sales grew 4.4% (vertically integrated) and 10.3% (T&D) y/y, driven by strong commercial and industrial load growth including data-center and hyperscaler demand.
Segment GAAP earnings show AEP Transmission Holdco falling to $225M from $578M y/y, the single largest driver of the consolidated EBIT decline, tied to the non-recurring 2025 items noted above.
A higher weighted-average share count (544M vs 534M shares y/y) modestly compounded the per-share decline beyond the drop in total net income.

AEP raised FY2026 operating EPS guidance to $6.25-$6.55 from $6.15-$6.45 on strong first-half results, reaffirmed its 7%-9% long-term growth rate, and highlighted 69 GW of contracted load growth through 2030 and ~13 GW of secured gas turbine capacity.
